query:
Two group members respond to the kiln shelf arrangement for the upcoming firing. One of them uses iron oxide wash on their stoneware and dismissed concerns about contamination; the other is the one who asked for a separate shelf because of surface sensitivity in their porcelain pieces. Which of these positions belongs to Reuben?

Options:
A. Callum
B. Reuben
C. Nadia
D. Yuki
context:
[1] (about=Reuben, episodic, t0 @2026-01-18T10:46:00) Fair enough. Though technically speaking the iron oxide wash fires clean at that cone -- not much contamination risk. But separate shelves are good practice.
[2] (about=Callum, episodic, t0 @2026-01-18T10:41:00) On the subject of the kiln load -- I want to make sure the porcelain mugs go on their own shelf if possible. I learnt last year that stoneware dust in the same firing can affect the surface. Not a disaster, but it shows on the translucent pieces. Would that be feasible, Nadia?
[3] (about=Nadia, episodic, t0 @2026-01-18T10:44:00) yes, easy -- I'll put your shelf at the top, temperature's more even there anyway and it's away from Reuben's oxide pieces. good call. 👍
[4] (about=Nadia, episodic, t6 @2026-04-12T09:59:00) yes, I've booked the kiln for a glaze fire after the session -- we can do your test tiles and I'll put my gas-kiln pieces in for the full fire if there's space. your shelf goes on top, same as last time. 🔥
[5] (about=Reuben, episodic, t4 @2026-03-15T10:12:00) Callum's right that matched sets need consistency. Technically speaking, that's exactly why porcelain in reduction is quite difficult -- you'd need to load the kiln identically each firing to get anything close to repeatable. Fair enough as a constraint.

query:
In Sessions 6 and 7, Reuben credits someone's critique of his slab vessel for directing his revision work. Who gave the feedback that Reuben is acting on -- and how does the conversation make it possible to confuse this attribution with Nadia?

Options:
A. Nadia
B. Simone
C. Yuki
D. Callum
context:
[1] (about=Reuben, episodic, t10 @2026-06-14T10:16:00) Slab work. I want to resolve the lower third on the vessel Yuki mentioned last month. Technically speaking, the texture transition is the issue -- I've been thinking about it since she said it and she was right.
[2] (about=Yuki, episodic, t8 @2026-05-17T10:39:00) Reuben asked for my opinion on the slab piece he brought last month. I said it worked. I think I was wrong not to say more at the time.
[3] (about=Reuben, episodic, t8 @2026-05-17T10:44:00) That is exactly what I needed to hear. Thank you.
[4] (about=Reuben, episodic, t8 @2026-05-17T10:41:00) I appreciated what you did say. You could say more now if you have it.
[5] (about=Simone, episodic, t10 @2026-06-14T10:30:00) the vibes on unpredictable glazes are incredible, Nadia said the same about the gas kiln 🌈
[6] (about=Nadia, episodic, t10 @2026-06-14T10:33:00) that is not what I said about the gas kiln, Simone -- I said I grew to love the unpredictability after I stopped fighting it. you have to understand the process before you lean into the variation. just test the tile first, okay? 🙏
[7] (about=Callum, core, t2 @2026-02-15T09:51:00) accepte le retour de Reuben sur le pied étroit de son mug : la fonction doit primer sur l'esthétique pour la vaisselle.
[8] (about=Callum, said_by=Reuben, profile, t4 @2026-03-15T09:59:00) Reuben note que Callum a raison que les ensembles assortis nécessitent de la cohérence, et que la porcelaine en réduction est difficile car il faut charger le four de manière identique à chaque cuisson.
[9] (about=Nadia, core, t14 @2026-08-23T09:57:00) vient à la création différemment de Reuben : elle a parfois besoin de faire la surface pour comprendre la forme, car elle tourne et la relation entre l'argile et l'outil est plus immédiate pour elle, alors que le travail à la plaque est plus délibéré dès le départ.
[10] (about=Reuben, said_by=Yuki, profile, t12 @2026-07-19T09:49:00) Yuki a approuvé la décision de Reuben de recommencer la section inférieure de sa pièce en plaque.
[11] (about=Reuben, said_by=Simone, profile, t12 @2026-07-19T09:49:00) Simone a dit qu'elle respecte la position de Reuben sur le processus, même si elle ne ferait pas la même chose elle-même.
[12] (about=Simone, said_by=Reuben, profile, t12 @2026-07-19T09:49:00) Reuben a dit à Simone que son bol fonctionne parce que la forme est solide, la glaçure étant secondaire, et qu'elle n'aurait pas obtenu la forme sans les heures passées au tour.
[13] (about=Simone, core, t14 @2026-08-23T09:57:00) va réfléchir au commentaire de Reuben sur le plafond que crée son approche couleur-d'abord.
[14] (about=Yuki, core, t8 @2026-05-17T10:19:00) a donné un retour détaillé sur la pièce en plaque de Reuben : la section supérieure était résolue, le tiers inférieur ne l'était pas, la transition entre les deux textures nécessitait un autre passage, et dans l'ensemble la pièce n'était pas tout à fait aboutie mais proche.
[15] (about=Yuki, core, t8 @2026-05-17T10:19:00) a admis qu'elle avait dit à Reuben que sa pièce en plaque fonctionnait, mais qu'elle pense avoir eu tort de ne pas en dire plus à l'époque.
agent_answer:
The feedback Reuben is acting on came from **Yuki** (option **C**). She told him the slab piece’s upper section was resolved but the lower third was not, and that the texture transition needed another pass. Reuben explicitly credits **Yuki** in the raw excerpt: *“the lower third on the vessel Yuki mentioned last month… since she said it and she was right.”*

The possible confusion with **Nadia** comes from two things in the conversation: Nadia refers to Reuben’s vessel in the open-day logistics (“Reuben, you mentioned the large square vessel”), and she makes a process comment contrasting her throwing with Reuben’s slab work. Those remarks could be mistaken for design feedback, but they are not the critique Reuben is acting on.
